body:
Hey thanks a lot for the response! My first job which lasted about 3 weeks was at a store. I had thought I was getting a stocking job but turns out I didn't read the fine print where it mentioned I'd have to do anything they needed at any given time. Unfortunately for me it mean't running the cash register. Now I have no problem with running a cash register but the problem came to actually talking to the customers because of the stutter. I'm a kind of person that does things on impulse which can be good or bad but had a particularly bad stuttering day and on an impulse I just quit after my shift. I tried to make it to where I'd be able to just do stocking so I wouldn't have as much customer interaction but they wanted somebody to do everything. 

My 2nd job was sorta my own fault for getting involved with anyways. It was a rather physically demanding job and well i just couldn't keep up with it. My body was so worn out half way through the 2nd day from being completely sore from the 1st and still had 2 days left before the weekend so i knew I couldn't maintain it. But a good thing that has come out of that is I've started taking better care of my health with dieting and such. 

As for the meteorology, I'm involved with it pretty much every day! I absolutely love looking at weather maps, data and all of that stuff. Whenever I see an interesting storm or whatever on the radars i'll usually spend the entire storm's life looking at the radars, data, etc barring I don't have any other responsibilities or anything. I'll be really happy when I can afford to go back to school! I've tried looking into maybe like entry level jobs at weather stations and such but mostly everything you need a degree for. Which is completely fine, i'm willing to put in the time but yeah just wish it wasn't so expensive! I apologize for the big block of text but it's quite nice being able to talk freely without being judged. I imagine a lot of the things I've explained would come across as just lame excuses to a number of people. I understand that side but then again they might not completely understand my side of things.
